message.content:
**Los Angeles (Pacific Time) vs. Berlin (Central European Time)**  

| Period | Los Angeles | Berlin | Time‑zone offset | Difference |
|--------|-------------|--------|------------------|------------|
| **Standard time** (winter) | UTC‑8 | UTC+1 | 9 h | **Berlin is 9 h ahead** |
| **US DST only** (early spring) | UTC‑7 | UTC+1 | 8 h | **Berlin is 8 h ahead** |
| **Both DST** (late spring–early fall) | UTC‑7 | UTC+2 | 9 h | **Berlin is 9 h ahead** |
| **Europe DST only** (late fall) | UTC‑8 | UTC+2 | 10 h | **Berlin is 10 h ahead** |

### Why the difference changes

* **US daylight‑saving time** starts on the second Sunday in March and ends on the first Sunday in November.  
* **European daylight‑saving time** starts on the last Sunday in March and ends on the last Sunday in October.

During the overlap windows (roughly mid‑March to late‑March and late‑October to early‑November) the two regions are on different DST schedules, so the time difference shifts to 8 h or 10 h. Outside those windows, the difference is consistently 9 h.

**Bottom line:**  
- Most of the year Berlin is **9 hours ahead** of Los Angeles.  
- In the short windows when only one side observes DST, the gap is **8 hours** (early spring) or **10 hours** (late fall).

Usually, Los Angeles is UTC-8 standard, UTC-7 DST. Berlin is UTC+1 standard, UTC+2 DST. So difference: standard: 9 hours (Berlin ahead). During DST: Los Angeles UTC-7, Berlin UTC+2 => 9 hours difference still? Wait: -7 to +2 difference is 9 hours. Standard: -8 to +1 difference is also 9 hours. So always 9 hours difference. But if one is in DST and other not? Actually both observe DST but at different dates. So there are periods where difference is 8 or 10? Let's check: In US, DST starts second Sunday in March; ends first Sunday in November. In Europe, DST starts last Sunday in March; ends last Sunday in October. So there is overlap: from March 29 to March 31? Let's compute: In 2023, US DST starts March 12; Europe DST starts March 26. So between March 12-25, US is DST, Europe is standard: difference: US UTC-7, Europe UTC+1 => 8 hours difference. After March 26, both DST: difference 9 hours. Then Europe DST ends last Sunday of Oct (Oct 29 2023); US DST ends first Sunday of Nov (Nov 5). So between Oct 29-Nov 4, Europe DST, US standard: difference: US UTC-8, Europe UTC+2 => 10 hours difference. After Nov 5, both standard: 9 hours difference.

Thus time difference varies: 8, 9, or 10 hours depending on date. So answer: Usually 9 hours, but can be 8 or 10 during DST transitions. Provide explanation.
